test_cases.test_name: Verify Continuous Temperature Monitoring and Data Recording Intervals
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS continuously monitors temperature in GMP storage areas and records readings at intervals not exceeding 5 minutes.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are installed and calibrated in all GMP storage areas.
Access to EMS software interface and data logs.

test_steps.action: Observe the EMS software interface for a continuous period of at least 10 minutes, noting the temperature readings displayed for a designated GMP storage area.
test_steps.expected_result: Temperature readings are continuously displayed and updated on the EMS interface.
data_to_capture: Sequence of temperature readings and their timestamps

test_steps.action: Access the system's data logs or database and extract all temperature readings recorded for the designated GMP storage area during the observation period.
test_steps.expected_result: All recorded temperature readings are retrieved, and their timestamps are available.

test_steps.action: Analyze the timestamps of the recorded temperature readings to determine the interval between consecutive readings.
test_steps.expected_result: The interval between any two consecutive temperature readings does not exceed 5 minutes.

acceptance_criteria: Temperature readings are continuously displayed and updated on the EMS interface.
The interval between any two consecutive temperature readings recorded in the system logs does not exceed 5 minutes.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be recorded accurately and without loss.
Timestamps must be accurate and associated with each reading.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Temperature Range, Accuracy, and Alarm Deviation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS operates within the specified temperature range, maintains the required accuracy, and generates alerts when temperature deviates ±2°C from the setpoint.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Calibrated temperature monitoring probes are installed.
Access to EMS software interface.
Ability to simulate temperature changes or use a calibrated temperature source.

test_steps.action: Set a known temperature within the specified range (-80°C to +50°C) using a calibrated temperature source or by adjusting environmental controls. Record the setpoint temperature.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS displays a temperature reading that is within ±0.5°C of the setpoint temperature.

test_steps.action: Introduce a temperature deviation of +2°C from the setpoint. Monitor the EMS for alarm generation.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alert indicating a temperature deviation.

test_steps.action: Introduce a temperature deviation of -2°C from the setpoint. Monitor the EMS for alarm generation.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alert indicating a temperature deviation.

test_steps.action: Return the temperature to within the acceptable range (±2°C of setpoint). Monitor the EMS for alarm deactivation or resolution.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS alarm condition is cleared or resolved.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS displays temperature readings within ±0.5°C of the actual setpoint temperature.
The EMS generates an alert when the temperature deviates by +2°C from the setpoint.
The EMS generates an alert when the temperature deviates by -2°C from the setpoint.
The EMS alarm condition is cleared when the temperature returns to within the acceptable range.
data_integrity_requirements: Temperature readings must be accurate and within specified tolerance.
Alarm triggers must be reliable and timely.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Vendor Software Unmodified and Data Storage Format
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system uses vendor-supplied software without modification and that all data is stored in the vendor's standard database format.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Access to system logs and configuration files is available.
Access to the EMS database is available.

test_steps.action: Access the EMS system's software installation directory and compare file hashes/versions with vendor-provided documentation.
test_steps.expected_result: All installed software files match the vendor's original distribution without any unauthorized modifications.

test_steps.action: Query the EMS database and examine the structure and format of stored temperature and humidity data.
test_steps.expected_result: The data is stored in the format specified by the vendor's standard database schema.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS software is confirmed to be unmodified from the vendor's supplied version.
The format of stored environmental data aligns with the vendor's standard database format.
data_integrity_requirements: Verification of software integrity ensures no unauthorized changes affecting data recording.
Confirmation of standard database format ensures data can be reliably retrieved and interpreted.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Alarm Generation and Notification Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system generates alerts when temperature deviates from setpoint and that these notifications integrate with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is operational and monitoring temperature.
Site paging system is operational and configured for integration.
Defined temperature setpoints and alarm deviation thresholds are configured in the EMS.
Access to EMS alarm logs and paging system logs.

test_steps.action: Manually adjust a temperature sensor in a monitored area to simulate a deviation of +2°C from its setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system generates an audible and visual alarm for the specific sensor.

test_steps.action: Observe the site paging system for incoming notifications related to the generated EMS alarm.
test_steps.expected_result: The site paging system receives and displays a notification containing relevant alarm details (e.g., sensor ID, temperature, time).

test_steps.action: Manually adjust the temperature sensor back to within the acceptable range.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system clears the alarm condition and logs the resolution.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-3 for a temperature deviation of -2°C from setpoint.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS system generates an audible and visual alarm for the specific sensor, and the site paging system receives a corresponding notification.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system generates an alarm within 30 seconds of a temperature deviation exceeding ±2°C from the setpoint.
The site paging system receives a notification for each generated EMS alarm.
Alarm notifications contain accurate and relevant information.
Alarms are cleared and logged appropriately when the temperature returns to the acceptable range.
data_integrity_requirements: Timely and accurate alarm generation is critical for preventing product excursions.
Successful integration with the paging system ensures timely notification of personnel responsible for corrective actions.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Standard Report Usage for Batch Release and Data Archival
test_cases.objective: To verify that standard vendor-provided reports are utilized for batch release and that data archival functions correctly.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
Sufficient historical data exists to test archival.
Access to vendor's standard reporting module.

test_steps.action: Generate a standard report for a specific batch using the vendor's built-in reporting functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates the report in the vendor's standard format, containing accurate historical temperature and humidity data.

test_steps.action: Initiate the data archival process for data older than the defined retention period (e.g., 7 years).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully archives the specified historical data using its built-in archival feature, without impacting current system operation.
data_to_capture: Archival process start and end timestamps

test_steps.action: Attempt to access archived data to confirm its integrity and availability.
test_steps.expected_result: Archived data is retrievable and remains intact, demonstrating successful archival.

acceptance_criteria: Standard reports are generated accurately and in the vendor's specified format.
Data archival process completes successfully.
Archived data is retrievable and maintains its integrity.
data_integrity_requirements: Data accuracy in reports
Completeness of archived data
Data retrievability after archival

test_cases.test_name: Verify Electronic Signature Functionality and Audit Trail Compliance
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system's electronic signature functionality meets 21 CFR Part 11 requirements and that the audit trail captures all relevant events.
prerequisites: EMS system is installed and configured.
User accounts with appropriate permissions are created.
Access to audit trail logs.

test_steps.action: Perform an action requiring an electronic signature (e.g., approving a report, acknowledging an alarm).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for and captures a valid electronic signature using the vendor's built-in functionality, including user ID, password, and timestamp.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail to confirm that the electronic signature event and other critical system actions (e.g., login, data changes, alarm acknowledgments) are logged.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail contains a comprehensive record of all user actions, system events, and electronic signatures, including date, time, user, and event description.

test_steps.action: Attempt to tamper with or delete audit trail entries.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents tampering or deletion of audit trail entries, ensuring data integrity.

acceptance_criteria: Electronic signatures are captured accurately and in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11.
The audit trail logs all critical system events and user actions.
Audit trail entries are protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
data_integrity_requirements: Uniqueness and authenticity of electronic signatures
Completeness and immutability of audit trail
Timestamp accuracy

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage Capacity and System Availability
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system has sufficient data storage capacity for 10 years and meets the required availability of 99.5%.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and operational.
Access to system logs and configuration settings.
Knowledge of system maintenance schedules.

test_steps.action: Review system configuration and database settings to determine current data storage capacity and projected usage rate.
test_steps.expected_result: System configuration clearly indicates data storage capacity and a method to estimate data growth.

test_steps.action: Analyze system logs and uptime reports over a defined period (e.g., 1 month) to calculate system availability.
test_steps.expected_result: System availability is calculated to be >= 99.5% excluding documented planned maintenance periods.
data_to_capture: Dates and durations of planned maintenance

test_steps.action: Project data storage needs for 10 years based on current usage rates and system configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: Calculated storage requirement for 10 years is within the system's designed capacity or a plan for expansion is documented.

acceptance_criteria: System data storage capacity is confirmed to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
System availability is verified to be at least 99.5% over the observed period, excluding planned maintenance.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate calculation of storage needs.
Reliable logging of system uptime and downtime.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Facility Management System and Paging System Integration
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system can successfully interface with the existing facility management system and integrate alarm notifications with the site paging system.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and operational.
Facility Management System (FMS) is operational and accessible.
Site paging system is operational and accessible.
Vendor API documentation for alarm notifications is available.
Network connectivity between systems is established.

test_steps.action: Configure the EMS system to send data points (e.g., temperature, humidity) to the FMS via standard protocols.
test_steps.expected_result: Data points from the EMS are successfully received and displayed in the FMS in the expected format.
data_to_capture: Sample data points received by FMS
Screenshots of FMS displaying EMS data

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature alarm condition within the EMS that would trigger an alert.
test_steps.expected_result: The EMS generates an alarm notification.
data_to_capture: Alarm details (e.g., sensor ID, value, setpoint)

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification is sent to the site paging system using the vendor API.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is received by the site paging system and delivered to the designated personnel.
data_to_capture: Confirmation of receipt by paging system (if available)
Test page received by designated personnel

test_steps.action: Verify that the alarm notification response time from the EMS to the paging system meets the specified requirement.
test_steps.expected_result: The time from alarm generation to notification delivery via paging system is within the defined system response time (URS-EMS-011).

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system successfully interfaces with the FMS, transmitting critical environmental data.
Alarm notifications generated by the EMS are successfully transmitted to the site paging system.
Alarm notification response time meets the requirement of 30 seconds.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-014: System shall interface with existing facility management system via standard protocols.
URS-EMS-015: Alarm notifications shall integrate with site paging system using vendor API.
URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions.
data_integrity_requirements: Accurate transmission of data to FMS.
Timely and accurate delivery of alarm notifications.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Response Time for Alarm Conditions
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system responds to alarm conditions within the specified time limit.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and configured.
Temperature sensors are calibrated and operational.
Alarm setpoints are configured correctly.

test_steps.action: Induce a temperature deviation that triggers an alarm condition in a monitored area.
test_steps.expected_result: An alarm notification is generated by the EMS system.

test_steps.action: Measure the time elapsed from the moment the temperature deviation occurred to the generation of the alarm notification.
test_steps.expected_result: The system response time for the alarm condition does not exceed 30 seconds.

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system generates an alarm notification within 30 seconds of a temperature deviation exceeding the setpoint by ±2°C.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-011: System response time shall not exceed 30 seconds for alarm conditions.
data_integrity_requirements: Alarm timestamps must be accurate and unalterable.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Data Storage Capacity and System Availability
test_cases.objective: To verify that the EMS system has sufficient data storage capacity for 10 years of monitoring and maintains the required availability.
prerequisites: EMS system is fully installed and configured.
System has been running for a sufficient period to simulate data accumulation.
Access to system logs and monitoring tools.

test_steps.action: Review system logs and configuration to determine the current data storage utilization and estimate future growth based on monitoring frequency.
test_steps.expected_result: The system's current storage capacity and estimated future usage indicate it can support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.

test_steps.action: Monitor system uptime over a defined period (e.g., 1 week) excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
test_steps.expected_result: The system availability is calculated to be 99.5% or higher.
data_to_capture: Total uptime during the monitoring period
Total downtime during the monitoring period

acceptance_criteria: The EMS system's data storage capacity is sufficient to support a minimum of 10 years of continuous monitoring.
The EMS system achieves an availability of 99.5% or higher, excluding planned maintenance.
regulatory_basis: URS-EMS-012: Data storage capacity shall support minimum 10 years of continuous monitoring.
URS-EMS-013: System availability shall be 99.5% excluding planned maintenance.
data_integrity_requirements: Data must be retained for the specified duration without corruption or loss.
